title: WE WILL GO WHERE YOU SEND US

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then they answered Joshua, "Whatever you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go. Just as we fully obeyed Moses, so we will obey you. Only may the Lord your God be with you as he was with Moses. Whoever rebels against your word and does not obey it, whatever you may command them, will be put to death. Only be strong and courageous!" — Josh 1:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with the people's whole-hearted response. They pledge full obedience and, touchingly, they echo God's own words back to their leader: "Only be strong and courageous!" The encouragement God gave to Joshua, the people now give to him. God often strengthens us through the words of others.

We should read their words about the death penalty honestly, not skip over them. Israel was a nation under God's direct covenant rule, and rebellion during this holy mission was treated as rebellion against God Himself. This was a specific arrangement for that covenant people at that time; it is not a pattern for how we treat those who disagree with leaders today. We must not lift such laws out of their setting and apply them where they were never meant to go.

Yet a timeless truth remains: obedience and unity mattered deeply to God, and they still do. A people pulling together under God's appointed direction can accomplish what a divided people never could.

Their promise, "wherever you send us we will go," finds its fullest echo in Christ, who said, "Not my will, but yours be done" (Luke 22:42). And our surrender to Him is safe, because the One we follow always leads us in love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Whose God-given encouragement could you offer to someone today?
2. Is there an area where God is asking, "Will you go wherever I send you?"
3. How does Christ's own surrender to the Father help you trust and obey?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make my heart say, "Wherever You send me, I will go." Give me a spirit of glad obedience and unity with Your people. Amen.
